title: CRISPR deactivation in mammalian cells using photocleavable guide RNAs
protocol: Anneal light-deactivatable pcRNA with tracrRNA.
Combine 1.2 μL of pcRNA targeting DNMT3B with 1.2 μL of tracrRNA in a PCR tube to form 2.4 μL of 50 μM annealed gRNA.
Mix by pipetting up and down 5–10 times.
Heat at 95°C in thermocycler for 3 min.
Cool on benchtop (room temperature; 20°C) for 5 min.
Add Cas9 to the annealed gRNA.
Mix by pipetting up and down 5–10 times.
Add PBS, then mix again by pipetting.
Open the Lonza SF kit.
Combine 16.4 μL of SF nucleofection reagent with 3.6 μL of Supplement 1 in a separate tube.
Mix by pipetting up and down 5–10 times to form 20 μL of mixed nucleofection reagent.
Proceed to prepare cells for electroporation in cell culture hood.
Dissociate the cells using Trypsin.
Mix dissociated cells to achieve a single-cell suspension before electroporation.
Pellet the single cell suspension and resuspend in 1 mL PBS.
Mix the cell pellet with RNP solution thoroughly.
Set up electroporation settings on the Lonza electroporator.
Begin the electroporation after placing the cuvette in the machine.
Prepare 48-well plates with collagen.
Mix 10 μL of collagen with 1 mL of ice-cold PBS to create a 1:100 collagen solution.
Add approximately 0.3 mL of the 1:100 collagen solution to cover three wells in a 48-well plate.
Incubate the plates containing collagen at 37°C in a cell culture incubator for 10 minutes.
Remove the collagen solution from the wells after incubation.
Let the wells dry in the cell culture hood with the lid slightly open.
Aspirate the medium from cells grown to 60%–90% confluency on 1:100 collagen-coated plates.
Heat DMEM complete, PBS, and 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA in a 37°C water bath until solutions reach 37°C (takes at least 10 minutes).
Prepare approximately 800,000 HEK293T cells for electroporation.
Add enough pre-warmed 0.05% Trypsin-EDTA into the culture flask to completely cover cells.
Incubate for 5 minutes in a 37°C cell culture incubator to fully dissociate cells.
Add equal volumes of DMEM complete, gently mix by pipetting 5–10 times to create a single cell suspension.
Collect the cell suspension into a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Count the number of cells using a hemocytometer under a light microscope.
Load 12 μL of cell suspension into each square region of the hemocytometer for accurate counting.
Determine the average number of cells in each square region and multiply by 10,000 to yield the estimated number of cells per mL.
Add the volume of cell suspension that contains 800,000 cells into a separate 15 mL tube.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 minutes.
Carefully aspirate the supernatant using a pipette without disturbing the pellet.
Resuspend the cell pellet with 2 mL PBS to wash cells.
Centrifuge at 200 × g for 3 minutes.
Remove as much supernatant as possible using a pipette without disturbing the pellet.
Perform a PBS wash to completely remove DMEM and trypsin before adding Cas9/gRNA.
Transfer the 20 μL mixed nucleofection reagent into the cell pellet to form ∼25 μL cell suspension.
Mix well by pipetting up and down 5 times.
Transfer ∼25 μL cell suspension to the 5 μL RNP mixture; add 1 μL Cas9 EP enhancer.
Mix well by pipetting up and down 10 times.
Transfer all (∼30 μL) to one unused well of the 16-well electroporation cuvette using a P20 pipette.
Carefully add the liquid to avoid formation of bubbles.
Select the cuvette well intended for electroporation in the machine touchscreen.
Next, select “Cell Line SF” from the list of options.
For the electroporation code, use CA-189 for HEK293T cells.
Press “OK” on touchscreen to confirm settings and proceed to the next screen.
Place the cuvette in the holder.
Confirm the settings and touch “START” on touchscreen to electroporate.
Place the cuvette in the nucleofector with the yellow pin visible on the side closest to the nucleofector body.
Label used wells for electroporation clearly, ensuring consistent orientation of labels relative to the cuvette.
Observe for white precipitate post-electroporation; its appearance indicates successful electroporation.
Note the green ‘+’ indicator as a sign of successful electroporation.
After electroporation, transfer to culture hood with lights off and add 50 μL PBS into the cuvette.
Transfer contents to an Eppendorf tube containing 250 μL PBS for a total volume of ∼330 μL.
Distribute 50 μL each to three wells (A, B, C) in a 48-well plate.
Add 300 μL “DMEM complete” media only to wells B and C.
Illuminate Sample A with a 365 nm LED flashlight for 1 min.
Add 300 μL of "DMEM complete" media to well A.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil and return it to the incubator.
Remove most of the media from well B using a pipette carefully.
Turn on the 365 nm LED flashlight, hold it 2 cm above well B for 1 min.
Add back 300 μL of fresh "DMEM complete" media to well B.
Cover the plate with aluminum foil and return it to the incubator.
Harvest genomic DNA (gDNA) from HEK293T cells.
Wash cells off 48-well plates with 200 μL PBS using a pipette or cell scraper.
Purify genomic DNA (gDNA) from cells suspended in 200 μL PBS using the DNeasy Blood & Tissue Kit following the manufacturer’s protocol.
Elute gDNA in 100 μL AE supplied with the kit.
Store purified gDNA at -20°C.
Measure DNA concentration using the NanoDrop 2000 UV-Vis spectrophotometer (optional).
Perform PCR to amplify the region around the Cas9 target site using forward and reverse primers HEKs4_F and HEKs4_R.
Combine reagents for PCR reaction.
Mix by pipetting up and down 5–10 times.
Start thermocycling protocol (for HEKs4_F/HEKs4_R primer set).
Extract PCR-amplified target DNA using QIAquick PCR Purification Kit following manufacturer’s protocol.
Add 50 μL PB to the PCR product, then add 10 μL of 3 M NaAc and mix using a pipette.
Load the mixture onto a spin column and centrifuge at 17,900 × g for 1 minute.
Decant the collection tube and discard the flow-through.
Add 750 μL PE to the spin column and centrifuge at 17,900 × g for 1 minute.
Discard the collection tube and perform another dry spin of the column at 17,900 × g for 1 minute.
Elute DNA in 30 μL EB.
Measure DNA concentration using NanoDrop 2000 UV-Vis spectrophotometer (optional).
Run PCR product on gel electrophoresis to yield a band of expected size (optional).
Submit 10 μL of the PCR product for Sanger Sequencing using Fwd and/or Rev PCR primer as sequencing primer.
Sequence wild type HEK293T cells for “negative control” sample with no genome editing.
Pause point: continue with Sanger sequencing analysis any time.
Evaluate genome editing efficiencies from Sanger sequencing results using TIDE: Tracking of Indels by DEcomposition.
Obtain Sanger sequencing reads in .ab extension format.
Directly visualize the Sanger sequencing traces using a program such as SnapGene.
Visit the TIDE website.
Enter GGCACTGCGGCTGGAGGTGG as the guide sequence for HEK site 4.
Enter the .ab sequencing file for the negative control under “Control Sample Chromatogram (.ab1 or .scf)”.
Enter the .ab sequencing file for the intended sample under “Test Sample Chromatogram (.ab1 or .scf)”.
Press the blue “Update View” button.
